In 1970, Oregon had a dead whale problem. So they decided to blow it up.
A huge sperm whale had washed up on a beach in Florence, and the smell was unbearable.
Oregon's beaches counted as highways, so the job went to the highway department.
Their plan? Half a ton of dynamite.
The blast would turn the whale into tiny pieces, and seagulls would clean up the rest.
A crowd gathered to watch. News cameras were rolling.
Chunks of whale flew hundreds of meters, and rained down on the crowd.
One huge piece crushed the roof of a brand new car.
The seagulls were scared away. And most of the whale was still on the beach.
Today, Florence has a park named after it. Exploding Whale Memorial Park.
